name: Streaming algorithm quality improvement (vs batch reference)

description: Baseline: streaming PV-only vs batch hybrid reference

asi.key_gap: percussive content at 268/1000 vs harmonic at 636/1000

description: Mono transient detection + phase reset in streaming path — no improvement detected

asi.hypothesis: Adding mono transient detection/phase resets to streaming PV would improve percussive quality
asi.rollback_reason: No measurable improvement — transient scheduler warmup consumes initial frames and detection thresholds may be too high for synthetic percussive signal. Also PV phase reset alone can't match WSOLA transient preservation.
asi.next_action_hint: Try halving PV hop size in streaming to match batch quality (batch uses hop_size/2). Or try different approach: improve spectral similarity rather than trying to match hybrid output.
asi.insight: streaming uses params.hop_size while batch uses params.hop_size/2 — this is the biggest parameter difference between streaming and batch PV

description: Use half-hop PV in streaming to match batch PV quality (hop_size/2)

asi.hypothesis: Batch hybrid uses hop_size/2 for PV, streaming used hop_size. Matching should improve quality.
asi.result: Only +1.0 quality_score (+0.2%). Percussive improved 268.1→270.8. EDM and harmonic unchanged.
asi.insight: Half-hop alone doesn't significantly improve quality because the fundamental gap is WSOLA vs PV for transients, not overlap count. The PV with more overlap produces marginally better phase coherence but the waveform shape remains PV-characteristic.

description: Baseline with redesigned intrinsic quality benchmark (freq, energy, centroid, clicks, batch similarity)

asi.hypothesis: new baseline with intrinsic quality metrics
asi.key_bottleneck: streaming PV output has ~40-50% RMS of input due to OLA normalization, centroid shifts >20%

description: Attempted steady_state_window_sum normalization reference — no improvement

asi.hypothesis: Using precomputed steady-state window sum as normalization reference would fix energy loss
asi.rollback_reason: No measurable improvement — the normalization floor isn't the cause of energy loss. The energy loss is inherent to the PV algorithm: phase modifications cause destructive interference between overlapping frames.
asi.next_action_hint: Try: 1) Add RMS normalization as post-processing in StreamProcessor (simple gain compensation), 2) Focus on improving phase locking quality to reduce destructive interference, 3) Look at enabling envelope preservation in streaming which could help preserve spectral shape
asi.key_insight: Energy loss is from phase modification destructive interference, not from normalization bug
